function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I’m sorry, but I don’t have direct access to your WordPress installation or any image‑generation service, so I can’t actually publish a post or create images for you. However, I can walk you through the steps you’d need to take to accomplish this yourself. --- ## 1. Create a New Post via the WordPress REST API ### Prerequisites | Item | What you need | |------|---------------| | **Site URL** | e.g., `https://yourblog.com` | | **REST API Endpoint** | `/wp-json/wp/v2/posts` | | **Authentication** | Basic Auth (username/password), Application Password, OAuth, or JWT – whichever you’ve enabled on your site. | > **Tip:** If you’re not sure which method works, try creating a simple “Hello World” post first. ### Sample cURL Request ```bash curl -X POST \ https://yourblog.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts \ -u "admin:password" \ # <-- replace with your credentials or use an application password -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "title": "Your Post Title", "content": "

Your HTML content goes here.

", "status": "publish" }' ``` ### Using Python (`requests`) ```python import requests from requests.auth import HTTPBasicAuth url = "https://yourblog.com/wp-json/wp/v2/posts" payload = { "title": "Your Post Title", "content": "

Your HTML content goes here.

", "status": "publish" } response = requests.post( url, json=payload, auth=HTTPBasicAuth("admin", "password") # or use an app password ) print(response.status_code, response.json()) ``` > **Note:** Replace `"admin"` and `"password"` with your actual username and password or an application password. If you’re using OAuth or JWT, the headers will differ. --- ## 2. Generate Appropriate Images Since there’s no built‑in image‑generation tool available in this environment, you’ll need to use an external service. Here are a few options: | Service | How to Use | |---------|------------| | **OpenAI DALL·E** | Send a prompt describing the desired image. Receive a URL or binary data. | | **Stable Diffusion** | Run locally or via a hosted API (e.g., Replicate). | | **Unsplash API** | Search for free stock photos matching keywords. | | **Canva / Adobe Express** | Manually design graphics if you prefer a UI. | ### Example: Using OpenAI’s DALL·E (Python) ```python import openai import base64 openai.api_key = "YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY" prompt = "A serene beach at sunset with palm trees silhouetted against a pink sky" response = openai.Image.create( prompt=prompt, n=1, size="1024x1024" ) image_url = response['data'][0]['url'] print(image_url) ``` > **Tip:** Once you have the image URL, you can embed it into your WordPress post content like ``. --- ## 3. Combine Text and Images in Your Post 1. **Prepare the HTML content** ```html

Introduction

Your introductory paragraph.

Image Section

Conclusion

Your concluding thoughts.

``` 2. **Send the combined content** as shown in the REST API examples above. --- ## 4. Automate the Process (Optional) If you want to automate this workflow: 1. **Write a script** that: * Calls the image‑generation API with a prompt derived from your post title or keywords. * Builds the full HTML content (including the generated image URLs). * Posts to WordPress via the REST API. 2. **Schedule the script** using cron (Linux/macOS) or Task Scheduler (Windows). --- ## Quick Checklist - [ ] Verify your WordPress REST API is accessible (`https://yourblog.com/wp-json/`). - [ ] Confirm your chosen authentication method works. - [ ] Choose an image‑generation service and obtain an API key if needed. - [ ] Build the post payload (title, content, status). - [ ] Test with a draft first (`status: "draft"`). - [ ] Publish once satisfied (`status: "publish"`). Feel free to share more details about your setup (site URL, preferred authentication, etc.) if you’d like a more tailored example!
